eyebrow.zh: 本地 · 一行判定 · 单二进制

headline.zh:
一条命令看清
你的 Kimi K3 解码变慢是预热还是病态换出
headline.en:
One command reveals
whether your Kimi K3 decode slowdown is warmup or thrash

sub.zh: 挂到正在跑的 Kimi K3 进程上，按 token 采样磁盘重读率，对照 K3 拓扑算出复用比，30 秒内给出健康 / 部分 / 病态的一行判定。
sub.en: Attaches to your running Kimi K3 process, samples the per-token disk re-read rate, and prints a one-line verdict — healthy / partial / pathological — in about 30 seconds.

body.zh: 挂上去就开始按 token 给出磁盘重读率与滚动判定：健康预热、部分转暖、病态换出。不用等整轮跑完，也不用事后翻日志。
body.en: The moment you attach, it streams a per-token disk re-read rate and a rolling verdict — healthy warmup, partial warm, pathological thrash. No waiting for the run to finish, no digging through logs afterward.

chips: › 健康 / 部分 / 病态三档

title.zh: 一份能直接贴进帖子与 issue 的报告
title.en: A report you can paste straight into a thread or issue

body.zh: k3thrash report 把 trace 渲染成一段 ASCII：判定、重读率 sparkline、一行总结。贴到论坛、issue、聊天群，别人一眼看清你的 K3 在经历什么。
body.en: k3thrash report renders the trace into an ASCII block — verdict, re-read-rate sparkline, a one-line summary. Paste it into a forum, an issue, a chat group, and anyone can see at a glance what your K3 is going through.

title.zh: 挂到正在跑的进程，不重编译不重载
title.en: Attaches to a running process, no recompile, no reload

body.zh: 不用重编译 llama.cpp，也不用重载模型。找到你 K3 进程的 pid，k3thrash attach 上去就开始采——你正在跑的解码一行都不会被打断。
body.en: No recompiling llama.cpp, no reloading the model. Find your K3 process pid, run k3thrash attach, and it starts sampling — the decode you're already running is never interrupted.

title.zh: 本地运行，单二进制，MIT 开源
title.en: Local, one binary, MIT open source

body.zh: 一行 go install 拿到的静态二进制——没有常驻服务、没有云、不需要账号。个人自部署永久免费；多节点实验室的跨机对比是后续的事。
body.en: A single static binary from one go install — no daemon, no cloud, no account. Free forever for individual self-hosters; cross-node comparison for multi-rig labs is a later chapter.

headline.zh: 把模糊的「是不是在变慢」，收敛成一行可粘贴的判定
headline.en: Turn a vague “is it slowing down?” into a one-line, pasteable verdict

sub.zh: 开源、MIT、个人永久免费。诊断这一核心动作，永不设墙。
sub.en: Open source, MIT, free forever for individuals. The core act of diagnosing is never gated.
